key_insight: The paper characterizes when and how the mean of a Gaussian can be reliably estimated even when each sample is revealed only as the partition set that contains it, and it gives computationally efficient algorithms that attain (near) optimal statistical error under broad coarsening models.
problem_solved: Estimating the mean of a d-dimensional Gaussian with identity covariance from coarse / partitioned observations (each sample reported only as the cell of a partition that contains it), and understanding the fundamental limits (identifiability and sample complexity) plus providing efficient procedures that achieve them.
method: Formalize coarse observations as draws from a partition of R^d and derive information-theoretic identifiability and lower bounds that relate estimation error to partition granularity and dimension.

Design and analyze computationally efficient estimation algorithms (convexified / regularized likelihood-type and spectral/moment-based procedures) that exploit partition structure to recover the mean with provable sample-complexity and runtime guarantees.

Prove matching upper and lower bounds across regimes (when estimation is possible/impossible) and give robustness guarantees to realistic coarsening mechanisms (rounding, sensor bins, aggregated categories).
impact: Enables principled inference from widely encountered coarse or aggregated data (sensor bins, rounded measurements, grouped surveys), providing practitioners with concrete sample-size and algorithmic guidance to recover meaningful Gaussian means despite limited observation granularity.
visual_elements: Diagram: 2D plane partitioned into cells with true Gaussian samples shown and only cell labels revealed (illustrates coarse observation model).
Chart: Estimation error vs. sample size for different partition granularities (shows statistical rates and phase transitions).
Flowchart: Algorithm pipeline (data -> partition-aware estimator -> mean estimate) highlighting computational steps and complexity.
Table/infographic: Regimes of identifiability and sample-complexity summary (when estimation is possible, impossible, and corresponding guarantees).
paper_title: Mean Estimation from Coarse Data: Characterizations and Efficient Algorithms
paper_authors: Alkis Kalavasis, Anay Mehrotra, Manolis Zampetakis, Felix Zhou, Ziyu Zhu
